openQuestions.question: Does any supported deployed social-login environment disable mandatory MFA for password-signup owners? Auto-link by unverified signup email remains unsafe under that condition.
Are raw local media paths or object-store buckets reachable outside authenticated download handlers?
Does deployed ingress overwrite forwarded headers and prevent direct Gunicorn access?
Are Compose Redis/PostgreSQL host ports externally reachable and protected by authentication/firewall policy?
Which effective MFA policy and social-login providers are enabled? Conditional linking finding requires optional/no-enrolled MFA.
Do actual file workers/scanners and Windows connector-key ACLs satisfy the documented deployment guarantees?
Remaining source paths and AUD items are explicitly deferred; no complete repository, dependency or deployment assurance is claimed.
Public form normalization is recursive without an explicit depth cap and chat message fields lack explicit max_length; effective upstream body limits and concrete exhaustion impact remain unverified.

surfaces.label: Spoofed forwarded headers bypass anonymous rate limits
surfaces.notes: Authenticated throttles key by user. An ingress overwriting headers or trusted-hop configuration can mitigate. MFA is still required where configured. No independent per-account login failure budget exists in the inspected login path.

surfaces.label: Password changes accept unlimited MFA guesses
surfaces.notes: Current password is checked first, imposing hashing cost. Valid codes cannot be replayed. Challenges separately enforce failed-attempt counts. Existing session access is a prerequisite, not a newly granted capability.

surfaces.label: Imports update existing clients without client update permission
surfaces.notes: All matches are business-bound. Job locking, actor checks, validated mappings and terminal state checks are effective. Most fields must initially be empty; source must be OTHER. These constrain but do not authorize writes.

surfaces.label: Import previews disclose clients outside read permissions
surfaces.notes: Matches remain tenant-bound and require a supplied matching identifier. Only initial preview rows are used. No later job retrieval is needed to receive create-response duplicates.

surfaces.label: Cross-origin login can seed another account’s refresh cookie
surfaces.notes: SameSite=Lax prevents many cross-site cookie-sending flows but login does not need an existing cookie. MFA stops password-only completion for accounts requiring it. Frontend session-ID/user-ID checks reject changes when an old in-memory session exists, but storage.ts initializes both to null on reload.

surfaces.label: Ordinary members can hard-delete an unprotected business
surfaces.notes: Cannot choose a business without membership/support access. Payments, deals with protected references, support cases, billing offers and ownership transfers may block deletion. A newly created tenant with default roles/pipeline and only unprotected clients/tasks remains a valid path; PROTECT is not authorization.

surfaces.label: Read-only team viewers can claim privileged invitations
surfaces.notes: Existing-account invitations require the correct authenticated recipient. Tokens must be pending, unexpired and unrevoked; owner roles are rejected. Built-in owners/admins already have manage, so custom read-only permission matters. MFA enrollment for the new account can be performed by the claimant and does not restore recipient-only token secrecy.

surfaces.label: Merchant settings can clear a platform business restriction
surfaces.notes: Does not forge payment or directly grant a plan. Commerce gate, confirmed financial state, dates, subscription state/revision and plan terms still apply. The finding concerns the separate status boundary.

surfaces.label: An approved AI request can be reused for a different command
surfaces.notes: Tenant ownership cannot be changed; requester, approver's current authority and CRM object permissions still apply. Default owners/admins already approve, so the meaningful gain requires distinct custom permissions. Existing fingerprint tests changing only the tool do not cover writable approval state.

surfaces.label: Anonymous forms and chat can reverse another client’s opt-out
surfaces.notes: No campaign is sent by this operation alone. Tenant-bound lookup, active channel/form, conversation quota and public throttles constrain volume but do not establish contact ownership. Existing chat profile fields are preserved, but consent is still changed.

surfaces.label: Public intake responses expose private CRM identity relationships
surfaces.notes: Form returns only a boolean, not duplicate details. Chat creates a new random conversation capability and does not reuse existing conversation access. Active forms/channels, quotas and throttles remain; internal ID alone is not an auth bypass.
